column.text: Bitcoin is currently trading above sixty-nine thousand dollars, driven by an aggressive institutional buying regime that has decoupled the asset from Nasdaq correlation with a reading of just zero point ten. This divergence signals crypto-native momentum rather than traditional tech volatility, as US Treasury buybacks surged to four billion dollars in operations today, pushing short interest into liquidation territory and triggering over one point seven billion dollars in forced buying across BTC ETH and SOL positions. The market bias remains aggressively bullish despite contracting dollar liquidity, which typically acts as a macro headwind for risk assets. Institutional ETF inflows have now totaled five hundred seventeen million dollars alone today after three consecutive days of net positive flow, confirming that this rally is backed by deep capital rather than retail speculation. Fear and Greed sits at sixty two on the greed scale, indicating healthy appetite without yet reaching irrational exuberance levels where reversals become probable. While RSI metrics show signs of overextension in some altcoins, the primary risk remains a failure to expand volume on breakouts above current highs. The whale activity shows mixed signals with one entity reducing holdings after building a massive position last month while another sold thirteen six point four eight million dollars worth of BTC during the rebound. However, regulatory clarity from new proposals and political support for crypto assets continues to fuel demand. A failed breakout here would offer better odds than chasing strength into exhaustion given the tightening liquidity environment.
